title: finding(method): "declared but read by no renderer" is inferred from the absence of a `schema.KEY` read — unsound wherever the renderer FORWARDS its rest-spread onto the underlying primitive
body:
Filed by the `domain:spec` @ objectui execution seat (session `session_01QtGhnU3WnnWyiWeYQhw2aX`) out of the objectui#8236 flight, which **stopped before its first edit** because the card's central premise turned out false. The dev was barred from sweeping the class, so the class is filed from the seat rather than ridden on that card. Unassigned, bare, for triage — grading and `domain:*` are triage's.

## The inference, and why it does not hold

A whole family of cards is admitted on this shape:

> `grep -rn 'schema\.KEY' packages/` returns nothing in the renderer ⇒ the key is **inert** ⇒ ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove ⇒ retire it.

The middle step is unsound. `SchemaRenderer` hands a node's leftover keys to the component as **React props**, so a renderer can consume a key **without ever naming it**. A grep for `schema.KEY` cannot see that, and returns a confident zero.

Measured on `origin/main` `fff250f`:

`packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx:1576`

```
        ...componentProps,  // Spread non-metadata schema properties as props
```

`componentProps` is the rest of a destructure at `:1455-1481` that strips **16** metadata keys (`type`, `children`, `body`, `schema`, `visible`, `visibleWhen`, `visibleOn`, `visibility`, `hidden`, `hiddenOn`, `disabled`, `disabledOn`, `dataSource`, `_hidden`, `_disabled`, `responsiveStyles`). **Everything else on the node becomes a prop.**

## ⭐ The discriminator is a TWO-step read, and step one is not enough

Reaching the component is not the same as reaching the primitive. The renderer has to **forward** the rest-spread:

| renderer | destructures `...props` | **forwards it onto the primitive** | key is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `renderers/disclosure/collapsible.tsx` | `:22` yes | **`:23` yes** — `<Collapsible … {...props}>` | **LIVE** |
| `renderers/form/radio-group.tsx` | `:39` yes | **no** | inert |

⇒ ⛔ `grep -l '\.\.\.props'` is **not** the instrument either — both files match. The question is whether the rest lands on the underlying component, and that is a second read.

## The proof instance — objectui#8236, measured today

That card states `CollapsibleSchema.open` is "authorable on both declaration faces, accepted by the validator, and **inert**", and explicitly excludes the spread: *"The `{...props}` spread carries the **renderer's** props, not the schema, so it does not smuggle it in either."* Triage ruled retirement on that basis (comment 5571690998).

`open` is not among the 16 stripped keys, and `collapsible.tsx` forwards. Rendered through the real `SchemaRenderer` and the real registry, one fixture varying one key:

| leg | document | result |
|---|---|---|
| A | bare | `data-state=closed` |
| C | `open: true` | **OPEN**, body present |
| D | `open: false` + `defaultOpen: true` | **CLOSED** — controlled overrides default |
| J | `open: true`, click the trigger | still open ⇒ **trigger inert** |

A vs C is a two-polarity control: the only difference is the presence of `open`.

⇒ `open` controls the disclosure, overrides `defaultOpen`, and freezes the trigger. Retiring it would have withdrawn **working published behaviour**, and the tombstone's own remedy (*"author `defaultOpen` instead"*) is refuted by leg D — `defaultOpen` cannot express what `open: false` expresses.

## ⚠️ The repo already knew, in the file this lane reads most

`packages/types/src/__tests__/zod-mirror-parity.test.ts:1107-1108`, verbatim:

```
/** RUNTIME SLOT (objectui#6124): the `collapsible` renderer spreads leftover props onto the Radix `Collapsible` root. */
'disclosure.zod.ts#CollapsibleSchema': 'onOpenChange';
```

The sentence that refutes the card's exclusion sits in the parity ledger, under the same schema name. And it is not isolated: **29** `RUNTIME SLOT (objectui#6124)` entries in that ledger document this channel per-component (`calendar-view`, `chatbot`, `filter-builder`, `kanban`, …). Control: the same grep for a nonexistent marker returns 0.

⇒ The knowledge exists and is well-maintained; what is missing is that a card asserting **inertness** is not required to consult it.

## ⭐ objectui#6158 is the counter-example that sets the standard — ⛔ NOT an instance of the defect

Worth stating plainly, because the flight's report guessed the opposite and it is wrong: **#6158 (`RadioGroupSchema.orientation`) reached a TRUE conclusion with the RIGHT instrument.** It did not grep. It ran `next build` on `apps/site` and read the prerendered HTML, finding all eight radiogroup roots byte-identical with no `data-orientation` emitted. The finding held; PR #6244 forwarded the key and the card closed `completed` on 2026-08-25.

⇒ The remedy this card is pointing at already has a worked precedent in the repo. #6158 is what an inertness claim is supposed to look like.

## Population — a BOUND, ⛔ not an enumeration

`packages/components/src/renderers/**`: **83 of 185** `.tsx` files contain `...props`. That is an **upper bound** on the at-risk set, not the set — `radio-group.tsx` is in the 83 and is not at risk. ⚠️ **The at-risk subset (destructure AND forward) is NOT enumerated here**; doing it needs the two-step read above, and one number without that read would be exactly the kind of confident count this card is about.

⚠️ Equally unmeasured, and stated rather than implied: **objectui#5667** (`CalendarViewSchema` declares 9 of 13 keys said to be unread) is named in #8236 as a sibling but **I have not measured it**, and I am not asserting it is affected.

## Worth considering — raising, ⛔ not proposing

Any of these is a ruling, not a mechanical fix:

1. A **standing evidentiary rule**: a card claiming a declared key is inert must carry a runtime reading (rendered DOM or a real-`SchemaRenderer` probe), not a source grep — the #6158 standard, written down.
2. A `scripts/check-*.mjs` gate that cross-references declared keys against the strip list plus the forwarding renderers, so the ledger's `RUNTIME SLOT` knowledge is applied automatically instead of by a reader's memory.
3. Nothing structural; treat #8236 as a one-off and keep paying per instance.

⚠️ This class has now produced at least one ruling issued on a false premise (#8236), so the cost is not hypothetical.

## Not a duplicate of

- **objectui#4631** — the standing card that three declared surfaces (TS type / registry `inputs` / renderer reads) disagree with nothing reconciling them. That is about the surfaces **disagreeing**; this is about the **method** used to conclude one of them is dead. Closely related and probably wants reading together.
- **objectui#6124** — the runtime-slot refusal that names these keys on the mirror; it is the mechanism this card leans on, not the finding.
- **objectui#7353 / objectui#7804** — instances in the neighbouring family (declared-and-unread, and read-but-undeclared), not the method statement.
- **objectui#6158 / objectui#6150** — see above; #6158 is the counter-example.

Refs: objectui#8236 (the proof instance, released to `pm:retriage` with the readings in comment 5574448856) · objectui#6124 · objectui#4631 · objectui#6158 · PR objectui#6244.
